_what: Every substantive claim on this site, and the graph of what it rests on. A claim is only as good as the path from a measurement to it, and that path is usually invisible in prose.

_kinds.held: a dataset on disk, with its faults
_kinds.gap: data that exists but this project cannot reach, or that nobody has measured
_kinds.synthetic: generated to test the method; licenses claims about the instrument, never about the world
_kinds.assumption: stipulated, not measured. The claim is void if it is wrong
_kinds.script: the code that does the work
_kinds.claim: a statement made on a page
_kinds.external: somebody else's published number, used as input

claims.claim: Every genuine water-chemistry row carries a clock value - the {calc:kemi_rows - kemi_startklok|,} of {fig:kemi_rows} rows without one are fragments of a broken note field, not samples. But a clock value is not always a time: of the surface-oxygen samples, {fig:det_clock_default} carry a filled-in default and {fig:det_clock_ambiguous} come from suppliers whose clock convention is mixed; {fig:det_n} can be placed against the sun.
claims.note: Corrects two earlier versions: one said no row carried a clock time; the next read the note fragments as samples without one. Neither looked at what the values were. scripts/clockzone.py tests every supplier and era at the summer-time changes.

confirmed.by: Claude (re-read against the new clock and Monte Carlo results, 2026-09-10; not yet read by the project owner)

claims.claim: Against sampling round the clock, the real schedule loses {calc@K-SCHEDULE-LOSS:(1 - det_rec_hi / det_even_hi) * 100|.0f}% of a sun-shaped daily cycle of size {fig:det_imp_hi} mg/l - and about the same share at every size large enough to recover above the noise.
claims.because: detectable.py recovers the same imposed cycle twice through the real estimator - on the real instants, and with each sample's hour redrawn uniformly over the day - and the loss is one minus the ratio of the two median recoveries. Only the hour differs between the runs. The share belongs to the stipulated shape: a cycle peaking at another hour would lose a different share.
claims.note: The round-the-clock side is a median over fewer draws than the real side. Does NOT claim the sea has such a cycle.

confirmed.by: Claude (rewritten from the forks' research and read against the METHOD_LAB wording: stance, reasoning and supports added, typed hours and the self-quoted note removed. 2026-09-11; not yet read by the project owner)

saw.said on METHOD_LAB.md: **The working day costs between 77% and 79% of a sun-shaped daily cycle**, steadily across a 4-fold range of sizes - every size large enough to recover above the noise.

claims.claim: If the surface daily oxygen cycle follows the sine of the sun's elevation, its size - the coefficient on that sine, which is more than its night-to-noon swing on any Danish day - is below {fig:det_limit} mg/l: a cycle that size out-spreads the archive in at least {calc:det_level * 100|.0f}% of noise draws, and every smaller size on the grid does so less often.
claims.because: The observed spread is measured on the real samples by the real estimator. Each size is imposed on the same samples over many noise draws and measured the same way. The smallest size whose recovered spread reaches the observed one in at least the stated share of draws is the bound: a larger real cycle would, in nearly every draw, have produced a larger spread than the archive shows. The true limit lies between that size and the next smaller one on the grid. It holds only if the cycle has the sun's shape and the noise is Gaussian of the measured size.
claims.note: A bound, not a value, and not evidence of a cycle - see C-ML-SPREAD-NOT-EVIDENCE.

confirmed.by: Claude (rewritten from the forks' research and read against the METHOD_LAB wording: stance, reasoning and supports added, typed hours and the self-quoted note removed. 2026-09-11; not yet read by the project owner)

saw.said on METHOD_LAB.md: A cycle of size 0.7 mg/l produces a spread at least as large as the observed one in 100% of draws, and every smaller size on the grid does so in fewer than 95% of them. So if the real surface cycle follows the sine of the sun's elevation, its size is below 0.7 mg/l. The size is the coefficient on that sine: the swing from night to noon it would give where the sun stands overhead, and more than the swing on any Danish day.

claims.claim: Nothing in the archive constrains the pre-dawn oxygen minimum, which is the value a threshold is about.
claims.note: Not a finding about the sea. It reflects when sampling is done.

assessment.counts_as: surface oxygen samples whose clock is an observed time, taken with the sun below the horizon - night and civil twilight - at a station's own position and instant
assessment.reasoning: {fig:predawn_night_n} night and {fig:predawn_twilight_n} twilight samples, of {fig:surface_o2_n} whose clock is an observed time. Spread across the whole record and all the stations that sampled, that cannot characterise a minimum at any one place.
assessment.confidence: High that the minimum is undersampled. The word 'nothing' is strong: the {calc:predawn_night_n + predawn_twilight_n|,} exist, they are simply too thin to constrain anything local.
assessment.would_change: Moored continuous sensors, or one season of deliberate pre-dawn sampling at a handful of stations.

confirmed.by: Claude (revised from fork w2-op's proposal and read against what it rests on: C-PREDAWN now rests on the observed sampling hours instead of C-WORKDAY and no longer states a motive; C-SIDIN and C-K1-BLOCKED lose the page history from their notes; each states its reasoning. 2026-09-11; not yet read by the project owner)

claims.because: G-PREDAWN counts the night and twilight samples among the surface oxygen samples whose clock is an observed time, from cycles.py's sun classes; clock_convention.json gives the hours at which samples were observed. The minimum falls before dawn, when almost none were taken, so nothing in the archive constrains it.

claims.claim: {fig:depth_borrowed} oxygen measurements at depth were placed in time with a clock borrowed from a same-day water-chemistry bottle; {fig:depth_none} had no bottle with a usable time to borrow from - none that day, or one whose clock is a filled-in default or of a mixed convention.
claims.because: scripts/depth_clock.py places a CTD oxygen measurement at the clock of the same station-day in the water-chemistry extract when that station-day has one unambiguous observed time, converted to UTC by scripts/clock.py; filled-in defaults and mixed conventions are not lent. Measurements with no such clock are counted and excluded. The borrowed count is taken after depth_clock.py's quality filters and the count with none before them.
claims.note: PROVISIONAL. The borrowing is unchecked, and G-CLOCK is what would check it. If casts systematically precede bottles, any diurnal pattern found at depth is partly an artefact. The two counts are not a share of one population: the first is counted after depth_clock.py's quality filters and the second before them, so their ratio is not the fraction that can borrow a clock. The second count grew when filled-in default clocks stopped being lent as if they were times.

confirmed.by: Claude (rewritten from the forks' research and read against the METHOD_LAB wording: stance, reasoning and supports added, typed hours and the self-quoted note removed. 2026-09-11; not yet read by the project owner)

saw.said on METHOD_LAB.md: 4,688,007 oxygen measurements at depth were placed in time with a clock borrowed from a same-day water-chemistry bottle, and 2,454,520 had no bottle with a usable time to borrow from - none that day, or one whose clock is a filled-in default or of a mixed convention. The two counts are not shares of one population: the first is counted after `scripts/depth_clock.py`'s quality filters and the second before them.

claims.claim: {fig:manure_14_businesses} businesses - {fig:manure_14_share_biz}% of the businesses with both animals and more than one declared hectare - hold register animal units above {param:harmony_1_4} DE per declared hectare. They hold {fig:manure_14_share_herd}% of the CVR-registered herd: a floor, because herds on businesses with no matched land stay in the denominator and can never count as above the line.
claims.because: scripts/manure.py joins the livestock register's animal units to the field-parcel register's declared hectares on the company number and counts the businesses above the line; the herd share divides their animal units by all CVR-registered animal units, so herds with no matched land stay in the denominator.
claims.note: QUALIFIED by C-DE-VOID: the threshold has no legal force. The harmony line is a retired legal ceiling, not a measured capacity of the land, and declared area is not spreading area; at the nitrogen-per-animal-unit conversion the incidence page states, the current ceiling sits at a higher line than this one. So this counts holdings above a historical marker. It does not show that their manure must physically leave the holding.

_figures: A claim may declare where its number came from. claims.py then reads the live value and refuses to write the page if the sentence no longer matches it. Provenance says what a claim rests on; this says whether it still does.
_basis: Every claim is COMPUTED - a script produces the number and records how it counted it - or ASSESSED: a reading or a judgement that no script can re-derive, assessed by a person in its 'assessment' field.
_live: No number is typed into this file. Claim, note, assessment and node texts use placeholders - {fig:}, {calc:}, {count:}, {read:}, {was:}, {param:} - resolved by claims.py when the page is built. See its docstring.

harmony_1_4.reason: The classic pre-2017 harmony limit, used by manure.py (LIMITS) as an indicator of manure pressure. It has no legal force now - see C-DE-VOID - and is used here as a physical indicator only.

flood_depth_min.reason: The depth from which floodgap.py counts a cell as flooded on land. The 2012 sheets also paint a thinner band below it, which this area leaves out.
